guidance: Listen once, then repeat immediately. Do not read the sentence before it plays.
Match the sentence stress and linking, not just the words.
The app scores word coverage; pronunciation is not machine-scored.

items.text: The library closes at ten on weekdays.
Students can borrow up to five books at a time.
items.tip: Link up to and at a time.

items.text: The new science building is next to the Student Union.
items.tip: Keep a steady rhythm across the place names.

items.text: If you lose your student card, report it to the front desk immediately.
The professor asked us to submit our essays before Friday afternoon.
Although the lecture was difficult, most students found the examples helpful.
items.tip: Contrast the two clauses with a small pause.

items.text: The university is planning to extend the library's opening hours during the exam period.
items.tip: Keep the long noun phrase together.

guidance: Listen for meaning first, then reproduce the sentence exactly.
If you miss a word, keep going instead of restarting.

items.text: The experiment produced results that surprised the research team.
Researchers collected data from more than two hundred participants.
items.tip: Link data from and more than.

items.text: The article argues that social media has changed the way people read news.
Students who review their notes regularly tend to perform better in exams.
The study found a strong connection between sleep quality and academic performance.
items.tip: Link between and sleep; stress connection.

items.text: Although the theory was widely accepted, recent evidence has raised serious doubts about it.
The report recommends that universities provide more support for first-year students who live off campus.
items.tip: Keep the relative clause attached to students.

guidance: Do not paraphrase. Repeat the exact wording.
Keep the final consonants clear.

items.text: The city plans to plant more trees along the river.
items.tip: Link plant more and along the.

items.text: Recycling is collected every Tuesday morning.
Many residents are concerned about the amount of traffic in the area.
The government has introduced new rules to reduce plastic waste.
Scientists warn that rising temperatures could affect food production in many regions.
If people use public transport more often, air quality in the city centre will improve.
The conference will focus on practical solutions for reducing carbon emissions in urban areas.
items.tip: Keep the long noun phrase together.

guidance: Aim for natural intonation, not robot-perfect words.
Keep the sentence stress on the message words.

items.text: The meeting has been moved to Thursday afternoon.
Please send the report to the manager by the end of the day.
The company is looking for someone with experience in customer service.
Employees are encouraged to discuss their ideas with their team leaders.
The training session will cover the new software that the company has just introduced.
Although the deadline was tight, the team managed to finish the project on time.
The survey suggests that flexible working arrangements can improve employee satisfaction and productivity.

guidance: Listen for numbers and place names.
Repeat without adding or dropping articles.

items.text: The train leaves from platform three at nine fifteen.
items.tip: Stress platform three and nine fifteen.

items.text: You need to show your passport before boarding the plane.
The hotel is a short walk from the main train station.
Visitors are advised to book their tickets in advance during the summer.
The museum offers free guided tours every morning except on public holidays.
If you arrive after midnight, you will need to use the side entrance of the building.
The tourism office has published a new map showing the most popular walking routes in the old town.

guidance: Keep technical words clear.
Match the speaker's sentence stress.

items.text: Please turn off your phone during the presentation.
The new app allows users to track their daily exercise.
Many students now use online platforms to submit their assignments.
The company has updated its website to make it easier to use.
Researchers are developing sensors that can monitor air quality in real time.
Although the device is small, it can store a large amount of information.
The workshop will explain how artificial intelligence is being used in medical research.

guidance: Answer spontaneously; there is no preparation time.
Speak for most of the 45 seconds and support your answer with a reason or example.
The tutor will not give feedback during the interview.

items.text: How do you usually prepare for an important exam?
Do you prefer studying alone or with other people? Why?
What do you do when you lose concentration?
How has your approach to studying changed since you started university?

guidance: Give a direct answer first, then elaborate.
Use specific details from your own experience.

items.text: What do you enjoy most about life at your university?
How do you usually spend your time between classes?
What clubs or activities would you like to join?
What advice would you give to a new student?

guidance: Explain how you use technology, not just whether you like it.
Include one concrete example.

items.text: How often do you use your phone for studying?
What technology do you find most useful in your daily life?
Do you think students rely too much on the internet? Why?
How might technology change the way people learn in the future?

guidance: Connect your skills to the job you want.
Give a reason for each preference.

items.text: What kind of work would you like to do after you graduate?
What skills are most important for that kind of work?
Would you prefer to work in a team or independently?
How do you deal with stress at work or school?

guidance: Use past tense for experiences and would for preferences.
Add a specific place or detail.

items.text: What is the most interesting place you have visited?
Do you prefer to travel alone or with others?
What do you usually do to prepare for a trip?
How has travel changed since you were a child?

guidance: Distinguish individual actions from government policy.
Give one example from your own city.

items.text: What do you do in your daily life to protect the environment?
Do you think individuals or governments should take more responsibility for the environment?
What environmental problem concerns you most?
How could your city become more environmentally friendly?
